title: Prime Number Checker
story: Prime numbers are the 'atoms' of mathematics — they can't be divided evenly by anything except 1 and themselves. You're curious which numbers are prime, so you build a function to check any number instantly.
why: The prime-checking algorithm combines while loops, modulo, early returns, and Boolean logic — a compact but powerful demonstration of everything learned so far.
analogy: Checking for primes is like trying to split a pizza evenly among different numbers of friends. If you can split it evenly (no remainder) with 2, 3, 4, or more friends, the pizza (number) is composite. If every attempt leaves a messy remainder, the pizza is prime — indivisible by anyone except yourself and one friend.
expected_output:
Not prime!
Not prime!
Not prime!
Not prime!
try_it: Optimize is_prime: instead of checking every number up to n-1, only check up to n/2. Can you figure out why this still works? Test with a large number like 97.
tips: n < 2 is not prime — handle this edge case first
Use `%` (modulo) to check for even division: `n % divisor == 0` means divisible
Early return inside the loop is efficient: stop as soon as you find a divisor
The loop goes from 2 to n-1 — you can optimize this later to sqrt(n)
common_mistakes: Starting the divisor at 1 — every number is divisible by 1, so you'd always return false
Forgetting to increment the divisor — infinite loop
Returning `true` inside the loop when a number doesn't divide evenly — you must check ALL divisors first
Considering 1 as prime — by definition, 1 is not prime
